items.passage:
A teaching office log records four sections given the same lab kit.
One: an introductory section at Harlow, autumn term, issued 4 September; by 27 November coursework completion ran 9 points above the same section a year earlier; demonstrator Danforth.
Two: an introductory section at Harlow, autumn term, issued 5 September; by 28 November coursework completion ran 6 points above the same section a year earlier; demonstrator Danforth.
The central syllabus set coursework at a third of the final grade, up from a quarter, and every section was marked to a frozen departmental syllabus. Completion rates cover the students in each section who attended every lab session, and every student in each section attended every lab session.
Three: an introductory section at Harlow, autumn term, issued 6 September; by 29 November coursework completion ran 11 points above the same section a year earlier; demonstrator Danforth.
Four: an introductory section at Harlow, autumn term, issued 7 September; by 26 November coursework completion ran 7 points above the same section a year earlier; demonstrator Danforth.
Rates were recorded to the nearest point and signed off by the teaching office.
items.notes: Check that all four sections share one distinct value on each of campus, course_level, semester and demonstrator. The closer neutralises the year-over-year comparison by holding assessment weighting, lab hours, the marking scheme and the syllabus fixed, which is what makes a before/after comparison adequate here.

items.confound_note: All four sections sit at Harlow in one autumn term, and a single change to the central syllabus covers every case at once. The mid-passage facts state that the central syllabus set coursework at a third of the final grade, up from a quarter, and that every section was marked to that central syllabus, putting the heavier share over every section whose completion was measured. Each section is compared against itself a year earlier under the smaller share, leaving the kit and the larger share moving together across the 6 to 11 point rises. The population and completeness clauses in the same line describe a tally with no gap between the students counted and the students the claim covers, leaving the syllabus change the whole of the defect.
items.notes: Cases must be byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. The confound works only because all four sections share campus and term.

items.confound_note: In cases one and three the completion figure was read before the kit was issued: 27 September precedes 4 November at Harlow, and 28 April precedes 5 June at Kelvinside. Half the evidence therefore describes coursework already finished when the treatment arrived, so it cannot speak to the kit. Only cases two and four are correctly ordered, and two sections are not enough to establish the claim.
items.notes: Closing sentence is verbatim identical to both TRUE items - the flaw lives entirely in the dates of cases one and three (4 November / 27 September, 5 June / 28 April), which is invisible to a bag-of-words classifier because the month tokens are simply swapped within each case. Check no shared confound is available: four campuses across four terms share no policy or timetable history.
